decisions.choice: Yes, after go-live. A Registry plugin (dinkus-ship, plus dinkus-ship-beta) built from the Ship repo root, replacing the old sandbox test plugin there, listed next to Commerce. It is a Block Kit mirror of hosted Ship: it keeps no label data and reads, quotes, buys and cancels through ship.dinkuskit.com on every click, so the two never disagree; Pitney Bowes keys stay Ship secrets. Sign-in: the owner pastes the same store key Commerce uses into the plugin settings; the plugin trades it only at dinkuskit.com/api/store-passes for a 5-minute Ship pass; the key never reaches Ship. Who: EmDash Administrators and Editors; lower roles do not see Shipping. The DinkusKit.com tick Print shipping labels in Ship governs only Ship's own page. Screens: a Shipping menu item listing paid orders waiting for a label, each with rates, Buy label, Print label and Cancel label, and the label state (No label; Label bought, with its tracking number linked to USPS; Label cancelled). Print label opens the label PDF in a new tab through a new Ship link that opens only that label for 5 minutes, reusable within that window. Refund questions, Settings, label history and connecting the owner's Pitney Bowes postage account stay on ship.dinkuskit.com, which remains the full version and fallback. Commerce is unchanged: its Create shipping label address stays Ship's, and once the plugin journey passes on the beta store, Ship forwards that address to the store admin's Shipping page for stores whose plugin has signed in. TEST orders get sandbox labels and a TEST banner as on Ship's page. Release: a new journey, Buy a label in the store admin, must pass on the beta store before the final release. Follow-up Ship change after the plugin: live tracking from the Pitney Bowes tracking webhook on DinkusKit's developer account plus a daily Track a Parcel check for undelivered labels, adding In transit and Delivered (live labels only; Pitney Bowes does not track sandbox labels).

decisions.question: Should Ship have a Registry plugin so owners buy and print labels inside the store admin, and what does it cover?
decisions.rationale: Ronald wants labels and tracking on the order inside the admin instead of two sites and two sign-ins. v1 used Ship's own page because Registry plugins draw only Block Kit, printing inside the admin waited on emdash#4049, and Commerce's backend.js is near the 128 KiB cap; a new-tab PDF through a short-lived Ship link removes the printing blocker. Shopify Shipping buys on the order page; Pirate Ship, ShipStation, Shiptheory and Shippo keep labels on their own site and write back. The mirror gives the Shopify experience while Ship stays the only label store. Keeps Pitney Bowes 2a (the owner PB sign-in never passes through the admin), the store-pass contract and hosted Ship sign-in, Registry caps (no plugin-to-plugin calls; manifest lists ship.dinkuskit.com and dinkuskit.com) and redirect manual. USPS-direct tracking rejected: a second business account, 30-day subscription renewals, no retries.

decisions.choice: A new store-pass scope ship:admin (audience dinkus-ship), issued by dinkuskit.com/api/store-passes under the store's existing Ship grant exactly like ship:orders; Commerce's ship:orders routes refuse it and it refuses theirs. The plugin's settings are the Store ID (siteId) and the store key, both from the Set up Commerce box, because store-passes needs the site_id in the body. Hosted Ship routes for the plugin: GET /v1/admin/orders, GET /v1/admin/orders/{id}, POST /v1/admin/orders/{id}/prices, POST /v1/admin/orders/{id}/labels (with by, the admin's email, kept as createdBy admin:<email>), POST /v1/admin/labels/{id}/cancel, POST /v1/admin/labels/{id}/print-link. The print link is GET /print/{token}: the session secret's HMAC seal over kind print, site, labelId and a five-minute exp, opening one label's PDF with no sign-in; a session cookie's payload can never open a label. The plugin's route is content:edit_any (Editors and Administrators), checked again in the handler. Nothing about the owner's Pitney Bowes account crosses to the plugin. Full table: docs/contracts/ship-plugin-v1.md.

decisions.question: What exactly do the Ship plugin and hosted Ship say to each other, and what does DinkusKit.com have to issue, to deliver ship-registry-plugin-001?
decisions.rationale: Ronald approved in the Ship plugin buildout thread, 19 Oct 2026 23:47 UTC ('lock it; merge 44'), after ClawSweeper cleared ship#44 head 3a5fdd7 with no findings.

decisions.choice: Pitney Bowes' tracking webhook, received at one Ship address for DinkusKit's developer account with a username and password PB sends on each update, plus a once-a-day Track a Parcel check for live labels not yet delivered. Each label carries a delivery state (in transit, out for delivery, delivered, problem) that Ship's order page and the plugin's Shipping page show; the plugin contract gains only additive fields. Sandbox and practice labels never get updates, so this is proved only on Ronald's real store with production postage, and Ship's final release does not wait for that proof. No Commerce change.

decisions.question: How does Ship learn where a live label is (In transit, Delivered) and show it in the store admin and on its own page?
decisions.rationale: Ronald's 'a a' on 20 Oct 2026 03:12 UTC in the Ship plugin thread (2a: build and deploy now, prove on the real store, final not held), on the 'Live tracking' recommendation in docs/decisions/ship-registry-plugin.md (19 Oct). PB's updates come with the developer account Ship already uses and cover every store at once; USPS's own subscriptions would add a second outside account and need per-number upkeep. The daily check catches a missed update (PB retries for 16 hours, then stops).

decisions.choice: The plugin keeps the 5-minute pass in its own KV beside a SHA-256 fingerprint of the store key and reuses it for later clicks only while the pass is under a minute old, has 30 seconds left and the same key is in the settings; a kept pass Ship answers 401 to is dropped and the call retried once. So a burst of clicks shares one trade, a newly pasted key takes effect at once, and a key replaced or a Ship turned off at DinkusKit.com stops clicks within a minute instead of at the next click. Hosted Ship is unchanged.

decisions.question: Does the Shipping page reuse its Ship pass across clicks, and how soon does a key replaced or a Ship turned off at DinkusKit.com stop clicks?
decisions.rationale: Ronald chose 'Accept 1 minute' on the decision card in the Ship plugin thread, 21 Oct 2026 01:12 UTC (options: one minute recommended, five minutes, drop the cache). A kept pass is reused for later clicks only while under a minute old, with 30 seconds left and the same key in the settings; a key replaced or a Ship turned off at DinkusKit.com stops clicks within a minute; only the store's own signed-in staff can use a kept pass.
